description: Hypothesis testing for location, variance, distribution fit and independence, together with linear, generalized linear and nonlinear regression objects that expose diagnostics, confidence intervals and residual analysis.

tools.name: LinearModelFit
tools.description: Fits a linear model in specified basis functions to data by least squares and returns a FittedModel object. The object can be evaluated like a function and queried for dozens of diagnostic properties. Use it whenever you need more than the bare fitted expression that Fit returns.

parameters.name: Weights
parameters.description: Observation weights for weighted least squares.

parameters.name: IncludeConstantBasis
parameters.description: False to force the fit through the origin.

tools.notes: Fit gives only the fitted expression; Design matrices and multiple predictors are supported by giving a list of variables.

tools.name: NonlinearModelFit
tools.description: Fits a model that is nonlinear in its parameters using iterative optimization, returning a FittedModel object. Starting values and constraints can be supplied to help convergence. Use it for exponential decays, sigmoids, peak shapes and physical models.
tools.usage:
NonlinearModelFit[data, form, params, vars]
NonlinearModelFit[data, {form, cons}, params, vars]
tools.notes: Always give reasonable starting values; poor ones are the most common cause of failure to converge.

tools.name: GeneralizedLinearModelFit
tools.description: Fits a generalized linear model with a specified exponential-family distribution and link function. It covers logistic, Poisson, gamma and other regressions in one interface. The returned FittedModel exposes deviance, residuals and parameter tables.
tools.usage: GeneralizedLinearModelFit[data, funs, vars, ExponentialFamily -> fam, LinkFunction -> link]
tools.notes: LogitModelFit and ProbitModelFit are convenient shortcuts for binary response models.

tools.name: LogitModelFit
tools.description: Fits a logistic regression model for a binary response, returning a FittedModel that predicts probabilities. It is the most common special case of a generalized linear model. Diagnostics and parameter tables are available as properties.

tools.name: ProbitModelFit
tools.description: Fits a probit regression model for binary data, using the normal CDF as the link function. It gives results very similar to logistic regression but with a different coefficient scale. Use it when a latent normal model is the natural assumption.

tools.name: DistributionFitTest
tools.description: Tests whether data is consistent with a specified distribution, or with any distribution of a given family. It returns a p-value by default and can report the full test table. Several test statistics are available through the Method option.
tools.notes: A large p-value means the data is not inconsistent with the distribution, which is not proof that it follows it.

tools.name: KolmogorovSmirnovTest
tools.description: Performs the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test comparing an empirical distribution with a reference distribution, or two samples with each other. It is based on the largest gap between cumulative distribution functions. Use it as a general-purpose distribution-free goodness-of-fit test.

tools.name: AndersonDarlingTest
tools.description: Performs the Anderson-Darling goodness-of-fit test, which weights discrepancies in the distribution tails more heavily than Kolmogorov-Smirnov. It is often more powerful for detecting departures from normality. It accepts a data sample and a reference distribution.

tools.name: ShapiroWilkTest
tools.description: Tests the null hypothesis that a sample comes from a normal distribution. It is among the most powerful normality tests for small to moderate samples. Use it before applying methods that assume normality.

tools.name: LocationTest
tools.description: Tests whether the location of one sample differs from a given value, or whether two samples share a location. It automatically chooses an appropriate test such as the t test or a nonparametric alternative. Use it as the general entry point for mean and median comparisons.
tools.notes: LocationEquivalenceTest compares several samples at once; MannWhitneyTest is the rank-based two-sample alternative.

tools.name: MannWhitneyTest
tools.description: Performs the Mann-Whitney rank-sum test for whether two samples come from distributions with the same median. It makes no normality assumption and is robust to outliers. Use it as the nonparametric alternative to a two-sample t test.

tools.name: VarianceTest
tools.description: Tests whether the variance of a sample equals a given value, or whether two samples have equal variances. Homogeneity of variance is an assumption of many other tests. Use it before pooled-variance procedures.
tools.notes: VarianceEquivalenceTest handles more than two samples.

tools.name: PearsonChiSquareTest
tools.description: Performs Pearson's chi-square goodness-of-fit test comparing observed counts with those expected under a hypothesized distribution. It is the classic test for categorical and binned data. Use it when data is naturally discrete or has been binned.

tools.name: IndependenceTest
tools.description: Tests whether two vectors of paired observations are statistically independent, choosing an appropriate method automatically. It covers both continuous and categorical data. Use it to check for association without assuming a linear relationship.
tools.notes: Related specialized tests: PearsonCorrelationTest, SpearmanRankTest, KendallTauTest, FisherRatioTest.

tools.name: SpearmanRankTest
tools.description: Tests for monotonic association between two paired samples using Spearman's rank correlation. It detects nonlinear but monotone relationships that Pearson correlation may miss. It is distribution-free and robust to outliers.

tools.name: SmoothKernelDistribution
tools.description: Builds a nonparametric kernel density estimate from data as a distribution object supporting PDF, CDF and random sampling. Bandwidth and kernel type are configurable. Use it when no parametric family fits well.

tools.name: HypothesisTestData
tools.description: Represents the full result of a statistical test, giving access to test statistics, p-values, degrees of freedom and formatted tables. Test functions return it when asked for "HypothesisTestData". Use it when the bare p-value is not enough for reporting.

tools.name: FittedModel
tools.description: Represents the result of LinearModelFit, NonlinearModelFit and related regression functions. Applying it to arguments evaluates the fitted function, while string properties return diagnostics such as residuals, confidence bands and parameter tables. Use it as the single object carrying an entire regression analysis.
tools.example:
lm = LinearModelFit[Table[{x, 2 x + 1 + RandomReal[]}, {x, 10}], x, x];
{lm[12], lm["AdjustedRSquared"], Short[lm["Properties"]]}
